LESSON: CHILDREN’S GOVERNMENT IN SCHOOL

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Citizenship and Governance in Kenya
Topic 5.5: Children’s Government in school
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Children’s Government in school, part of Citizenship and Governance in Kenya in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to have Children’s Government in school? 2. How can we support Children’s Government in school?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the composition of Children’s Government in school,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Children’s Government in school in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Children’s Government in school together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: learners develop teamwork skills as they share experiences in groups on functions of Children’s

Government in school.

● Citizenship: Learners develop information and communication skills as they communicate in different environments while discussing in

groups the composition of Children’s Government in school.

50

Values:
● Integrity: Learners display transparency as they simulate the children’s Government in session in school.

● Social Justice: Learners accord privileges without favour as they role play the functions of children’s government.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Humility and simplicity: Learners are able to relate with others and fit in groups as they discuss in groups the composition of Children’s

Government in school.

● Governance: Learners describe the functions of Children’s Government in school.

● Assertiveness: Learners respect other people’s views as they carry out mock election of leaders in class.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● English, Kiswahili and KSL as learners write a composition on ways of supporting Children’s Government in school.

● Religious Education as learners respect children’s government in school.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Braille resources,

• Approved textbooks and other printed or braille materials,

• Vetted digital devices with assistive technology
